subject: Amur Leopard
fact: Amur leopards have thick coats that help them survive cold winters.

subject: Javan Rhino
fact: Javan rhinos have a single horn and live in dense tropical forest.

subject: Sumatran Rhino
fact: Sumatran rhinos are the smallest living rhinoceroses and are covered with sparse hair.

subject: Black Rhino
fact: Black rhinos use a pointed upper lip to pull leaves and twigs from plants.

subject: White Rhino
fact: White rhinos have broad square lips that are well suited for grazing on grass.

subject: African Forest Elephant
fact: African forest elephants have straighter tusks and rounder ears than savanna elephants.

subject: African Savanna Elephant
fact: African savanna elephants are the largest land animals alive today.

subject: Asian Elephant
fact: Asian elephants have smaller ears than African elephants and a single finger-like tip on the trunk.

subject: Sumatran Elephant
fact: Sumatran elephants live on the Indonesian island of Sumatra.

subject: Mountain Gorilla
fact: Mountain gorillas have thick fur that helps keep them warm in cool mountain forests.

subject: Cross River Gorilla
fact: Cross River gorillas live in forested mountains along the Nigeria-Cameroon border.

subject: Western Lowland Gorilla
fact: Western lowland gorillas eat fruit, leaves, stems, and other plant foods.

subject: Bornean Orangutan
fact: Bornean orangutans spend much of their time in trees and use very long arms for climbing.

subject: Sumatran Orangutan
fact: Sumatran orangutans build leafy sleeping nests high in trees.

subject: Tapanuli Orangutan
fact: Tapanuli orangutans live in a small forest region on the island of Sumatra.

subject: Bonobo
fact: Bonobos live only in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and are closely related to chimpanzees.

subject: Chimpanzee
fact: Chimpanzees can use sticks and other simple tools to find food.

subject: Golden Lion Tamarin
fact: Golden lion tamarins have bright golden-orange fur and live in Brazil's Atlantic Forest.

subject: Cotton-Top Tamarin
fact: Cotton-top tamarins have a distinctive crest of long white hair on their heads.

subject: Philippine Tarsier
fact: Philippine tarsiers have huge eyes that help them hunt insects at night.

subject: Red Panda
fact: Red pandas use bushy tails for balance and to help keep warm.

subject: Giant Panda
fact: Giant pandas use strong jaws and wrist bones adapted like thumbs to hold bamboo.

subject: Snow Leopard
fact: Snow leopards have long thick tails that help them balance on steep rocky slopes.

subject: Tiger
fact: Tigers have striped coats and no two stripe patterns are exactly alike.

subject: Sumatran Tiger
fact: Sumatran tigers are smaller than many mainland tiger populations and live on Sumatra.

subject: Malayan Tiger
fact: Malayan tigers live in tropical forests on the Malay Peninsula.

subject: Iberian Lynx
fact: Iberian lynx have tufted ears and mainly hunt rabbits.

subject: Ethiopian Wolf
fact: Ethiopian wolves live in high mountain grasslands and often hunt small rodents.

subject: African Wild Dog
fact: African wild dogs have unique patchy coats and live in highly social packs.

subject: Dhole
fact: Dholes are social wild dogs from Asia that communicate with whistles.

subject: Addax
fact: Addax are desert antelope with twisted horns and broad hooves for walking on sand.

subject: Saiga
fact: Saiga antelope have unusual flexible noses that help filter dust and warm cold air.

subject: Przewalski's Horse
fact: Przewalski's horses have stocky bodies and upright dark manes.

subject: Grevy's Zebra
fact: Grevy's zebras have narrow stripes and large rounded ears.

subject: Okapi
fact: Okapis have striped legs and are close relatives of giraffes.

subject: Pygmy Hippo
fact: Pygmy hippos are smaller forest-dwelling relatives of common hippos.

subject: Bactrian Camel
fact: Wild Bactrian camels have two humps and can survive extreme desert conditions.

subject: Asian Tapir
fact: Asian tapirs have a bold black-and-white body pattern and a short flexible snout.

subject: Malayan Pangolin
fact: Malayan pangolins are covered in protective scales and curl into a ball when threatened.

subject: Chinese Pangolin
fact: Chinese pangolins use long sticky tongues to collect ants and termites.

subject: African Penguin
fact: African penguins make braying calls that can sound a little like donkeys.

subject: Yellow-Eyed Penguin
fact: Yellow-eyed penguins have pale yellow eyes and a yellow band of feathers around the head.

subject: Kakapo
fact: Kakapos are heavy flightless parrots that are active mostly at night.

subject: California Condor
fact: California condors have enormous wings that help them soar for long distances.

subject: Philippine Eagle
fact: Philippine eagles have powerful feet and a shaggy crest of feathers.

subject: Whooping Crane
fact: Whooping cranes are tall white birds with long legs and long necks.

subject: Spoon-Billed Sandpiper
fact: Spoon-billed sandpipers have small bills with spoon-shaped tips.

subject: Hawksbill Sea Turtle
fact: Hawksbill sea turtles have narrow pointed beaks that help them feed among coral reefs.

subject: Green Sea Turtle
fact: Green sea turtles are mostly plant eaters as adults and graze on seagrasses and algae.

subject: Leatherback Sea Turtle
fact: Leatherbacks are the largest sea turtles and have flexible leathery shells.

subject: Vaquita
fact: Vaquitas are small porpoises with dark markings around their eyes and mouths.

subject: North Atlantic Right Whale
fact: North Atlantic right whales have rough white patches called callosities on their heads.

subject: Blue Whale
fact: Blue whales are the largest animals known to have lived on Earth.

subject: Whale Shark
fact: Whale sharks are huge filter-feeding sharks with spotted skin.

subject: Great Hammerhead Shark
fact: Great hammerhead sharks have wide hammer-shaped heads that hold their eyes far apart.

subject: Sawfish
fact: Sawfish have long flat snouts edged with tooth-like structures.

subject: Axolotl
fact: Wild axolotls are salamanders that keep feathery external gills throughout life.

subject: Chinese Giant Salamander
fact: Chinese giant salamanders are among the largest amphibians in the world.

subject: Gharial
fact: Gharials have very long narrow snouts adapted for catching fish.

subject: Siamese Crocodile
fact: Siamese crocodiles are freshwater crocodiles from Southeast Asia.
